notes:
User is planning a November trip to Europe and seeking a central Paris hotel with an Eiffel Tower view, a fitness center, and breakfast included. Budget is approximately $200–300/night; location is flexible but central is preferred. They have enough Hilton Honors points for two free standard reward nights, possibly for a separate Las Vegas trip rather than Paris.

Paris candidates discussed: Pullman Paris Tour Eiffel (15th arrondissement; estimated $220–280/night), Novotel Paris Tour Eiffel (15th; about $180–230), Mercure Paris Centre Eiffel Tower, Hotel Eiffel Trocadero, and Hotel Le Walt. Pullman and Novotel were highlighted as good-value options. Hilton Paris Eiffel Tower was estimated at $250–300/night or 50,000–60,000 points/night, but exact November rates, point awards, availability, breakfast inclusions, taxes, and room-specific views must be checked directly.

Hilton Paris Eiffel Tower: in the 15th arrondissement on Avenue de Suffren, roughly a 10–15-minute walk to the tower depending on route. It has a fitness center, restaurants/rooftop bar, and some Eiffel-view rooms; not every room has a view. Earlier assistant claims about a 5–7 minute walk, 419 rooms, Le Jules Verne being in this hotel, room balconies, category, and made-to-order breakfast may be inaccurate and should not be relied upon. Hilton’s actual Paris property is generally Hilton Paris Opera; “Hilton Paris Eiffel Tower” may be a mistaken hotel name.

Breakfast discussion: Pullman buffet was described as offering hot eggs/meat, pastries/bread, cold cuts, cheeses, fruit, yogurt, cereal, juice, coffee and tea, with a modern relaxed atmosphere. Hilton’s was described as more extensive/elegant, with made-to-order eggs/pancakes/waffles and better service/views, but these details also require verification. Breakfast may be paid separately unless the selected rate includes it or the user has Hilton breakfast benefits/eligibility. User may be deciding between the Pullman and Hilton based on price, breakfast quality/variety, and atmosphere.

Separately, user was previously comparing Hilton Las Vegas properties, especially Hilton Lake Las Vegas Resort, Hilton Grand Vacations Club on the Strip, and Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas, and had requested Waldorf room/suite details. Exact current details and pric
trajectory:
User is planning a weekend getaway to Las Vegas and comparing Hilton properties. Main initial choice: Hilton Lake Las Vegas Resort, a more tranquil, resort-style property about 20 miles southeast of the Strip, with lake activities, pool/spa, dining, and access to nearby Henderson, MonteLago Village, Lake Las Vegas Village, Red Rock Canyon, and the Strip. They have enough Hilton Honors points for one free standard reward night and plan to redeem them; should verify exact points, dates, availability, taxes/fees, and resort fees because Hilton uses variable pricing. They have also considered Hilton Grand Vacations Club on the Strip (timeshare-style, larger suites, central location) and the Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas (luxury, CityCenter/Strip location).

Most recent interest: detailed Waldorf Astoria rooms and suites. The discussion covered Deluxe Rooms, Deluxe Strip View Rooms, Junior Suites, One-Bedroom Suites and Strip View versions, Premier One- and Two-Bedroom Suites, Waldorf Suite, and Presidential Suite. Key features described include king or queen beds, city or Strip views, separate living areas, marble bathrooms, separate tub/shower, HDTV, Bluetooth speakers, Nespresso, minibar, concierge service, sofa/chairs, dining tables, lounge access for the Waldorf Suite, and butler service for the Presidential Suite. Approximate sizes discussed ranged from 520 sq. ft. for Deluxe Rooms to 4,500 sq. ft. for the Presidential Suite. Actual room layouts, amenities, pricing, and availability should be confirmed directly with the hotel because prior details may be outdated or inaccurate.
